Long-Range Interaction Centrality (Maximal Path)

Source: R/centrality-batch61.R
centrality_lric_max.Rd

The long-range interaction centrality (LRIC; Aleskerov et al. 2017) measures the influence of a node on the others, directly and through chains of intermediaries. A group of nodes that send ties to \(j\) is critical when their weights sum to at least the quota \(q_j\), and a member is pivotal when the group falls below the quota without it. The direct influence of \(i\) on \(j\) is $$c_{ij} = \frac{w_{ij}}{\min \sum_{l \in \Omega(j)} w_{lj}},$$ the minimum taken over the critical groups \(\Omega(j)\) in which \(i\) is pivotal, and 0 when there is none. The influence along a path is the product of the direct influences on its ties, the total influence \(c^*_{ij}\) is that of the best path, and $$LRIC(i) = \sum_j c^*_{ij} u_j, \qquad u_j = \frac{\sum_k w_{jk}}{\sum_l \sum_k w_{lk}}.$$

Usage

centrality_lric_max(x, ...)

Arguments

x

Network input accepted by centrality.

...

Further arguments to centrality. The measure uses lric_quota (default 0.5), lric_path_length (default Inf), weighted and enumeration_limit.

Value

A named numeric vector with one score per node, in input node order, or NA at every node when the search was cut short.

Details

Direction and weights are used: \(w_{ij}\) is the influence of \(i\) on \(j\), and an undirected tie acts in both directions. Loops are ignored. lric_quota is the share of the weight entering a node that a group needs in order to be critical, 0.5 by default as in the example of the source. lric_path_length limits the number of ties of a path; by default (Inf) all simple paths are considered. The program of the authors limits paths to three ties, which changes some values. A node that sends no tie, or that is pivotal for nobody, scores 0. The scores follow the working-paper version of the source (arXiv:1610.05892); the published chapter was not consulted.

Finding the smallest critical group examines sums over subsets of a node's in-neighbors. With many distinct weights their number doubles with every in-neighbor. The measure is therefore costly, computed only when requested by name or through include, and it stops past enumeration_limit sums (default one million): every score is then NA with a cograph_undefined_measure warning. Parameters outside their domain raise a cograph_bad_parameter error.

References

Aleskerov, F., Meshcheryakova, N. and Shvydun, S. (2017). Power in network structures. In Models, Algorithms, and Technologies for Network Analysis, Springer Proceedings in Mathematics and Statistics, 79-85. doi:10.1007/978-3-319-56829-4_7 .

See also

centrality_con, centrality.

Examples

centrality_lric_max(regulation_net)
#>    Explore       Plan    Monitor      Adapt    Reflect    Discuss Synthesize 
#> 0.44265398 0.56901913 0.45503393 0.38191915 0.11378778 0.32237258 0.07273039 
#>   Evaluate     Create      Share 
#> 0.37815833 0.35995017 0.72519971
